title: Embed elasticity & versioning playbook with shadow-eval pipeline and rollback safety-net
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: define and implement a repeatable, low-risk onboarding path for new embedding models and safe deprecation semantics that preserve rank/quality and latency SLAs. This ticket covers: (1) an automated shadow-eval pipeline that collects side-by-side quality signals for new embeddings versus active variants, (2) traffic-shaping and staging policies to limit tenant exposure during rollouts, (3) compatibility shim strategies for dimensionality/normalization differences and hashing changes, (4) a rollback and telemetry-driven abort policy tied to SLO regressions, and (5) runbook content for PM/SE/customer communication when a model is deprecated or swapped.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow-eval pipeline runs on daily sample set and produces a quality delta report (cosine/AUC/precision@k) for each candidate model
Per-tenant canary policy exists: 0->1%->5%->25%->100% with automated pause-on-regression
Dimensionality compatibility shim is implemented for the common case (embed dim increase or decrease with right-pad/truncate + metadata flag)
Latency impact measured: 95th percentile token embedding extraction overhead does not exceed +12ms vs baseline for the candidate model under typical batch sizes
Rollback procedure in Console triggers immediate traffic switch and reindex checklist created for customers who opted into persistent indexes
Documentation (Console doc + internal runbook) published and linked in this issue
steps: Design shadow-eval dataset: combine production prompts (anonymized), existing internal benchmarks, and synthetic adversarial pairs
Implement offline runner that inserts candidate model calls in parallel with live calls (no routing change) and stores vectors + context for diffing
Extend telemetry to capture cosine similarity distributions, downstream rerank hit-rate, and per-tenant latency deltas
Implement traffic shaping controller: policy engine with percent ramp and automatic abort on defined signals
Build compatibility shim library: padding/truncation, L2-normalization toggles, and scalar rescaling utilities
Add API/Console UX for model aliases, deprecation timetable, and tenant opt-in for reindex jobs
Run closed tenant canary, iterate on thresholds, publish postmortem and SLA impact summary
notes: Trade-offs: full reindex for dimensionality changes is correct but expensive; default strategy is shim + advisory reindex for customers with persistent indexes. We prioritize safety (quality regressions) over immediate latency wins. Quantization differences must be flagged early in shadow-eval to avoid silent drift. KV cache interactions: new models with larger vector dimensionality can increase memory pressure — telemetry should track cache hit/miss and memory growth per host.
